lines.text: Today you will type your first real web page and watch the browser bring it to life.
Every web page is a text file written in a language called HTML.
Your browser reads that file and draws the page on your screen.
Every website you have ever visited started as text like this.
Tags are short words inside angle brackets that tell the browser what each part of the page is.
Most tags come in pairs, an opening tag and a closing tag with a slash.
The words in between the two tags are the content.
Heading tags make titles, from h1, the biggest, down to h6, the smallest.
Use just one h1 heading for the title of your page.
Then use h2 headings for each section of your page.
The p tag makes a paragraph of normal text.
The browser ignores extra spaces and new lines inside your code.
So every new paragraph needs its own p tag.
Anyone in the world can read a public web page.
Share your favourite things, but never your full name, school, address, phone number or photo.
A nickname is all a web page needs.
The Web Lab has two halves, your code on the left and the live preview on the right.
Every time you type, the preview redraws your page a moment later.
When you think you are done, press Check to see which goals you have reached.
Here is an opening h1 tag, the words Hello web, and a closing h1 tag.
The closing tag has a forward slash, which tells the browser the heading ends here.
The browser reads the file from top to bottom, one tag at a time.
The h1 is biggest, the h2 is a little smaller, and each paragraph sits on its own line.
Look at all those spaces and new lines inside one paragraph.
The browser squashes them into single spaces, so it all shows on one neat line.
Can you see the mistake? The closing tag is missing its slash.
The browser thinks the heading never ends, so everything after it becomes huge.
Add the slash, and the paragraph goes back to normal size.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
